checks: Verified the recorded digest of b0296f8a3b0d3d48 and checked the §4 one-coordinate argument and equation (7), including the constant-height improvement. The frozen proof makes the source's continuity assertion explicit and establishes the claimed boundary extension.

At an interior projected base, its open section is a bounded nonempty interval. Any point of the closed ambient set at that base is in the closure of the interval by interpolation with an interior point at the same base. Thus along any converging sequence of bases pointwise convergence of the zero extensions can fail only at the two endpoints, and bounded dominated convergence proves continuity.

Each normalized section CDF has strictly positive continuous derivative on its interval, so inverse differentiation gives X_i'=F_i u_i^β. The interpolated quantile is increasing and lies in the intermediate section. Weighted Hölder with factors F_i^(1/β)u_i and F_i^(−1/β) gives the stated lower bound for its mass integrand. When β=1 the quotient is a positive weighted mean of the two masses, at least their minimum. Substitution on compact quantile intervals followed by monotone exhaustion avoids any derivative assumption at the section endpoints.

A full tangent fiber together with points at affinely independent bases spans the base affine space times the tangent space, including a zero-dimensional base. The affine positive H,L and the perspective identity give initial β=m. Iterating in orthonormal tangent directions gives β=m−r and the final critical quasiconcavity. When H is constant, β=m+1 initially and β=1 after m strict integrations, giving convex reciprocal.

For an interior point of any projected contact set, the relative-interior section is nonempty by projection of relative interiors, and interpolation with its interior point makes it dense in the actual section. Its boundary is null in the integrated coordinates, so the open iterates equal the actual closed-section integrals there, including partially integrated ones. For r=0 the pointwise claim is the perspective inequality.

Contraction of the boundary fiber toward one point at a fixed relative-interior base gives the lower limit using the Jacobian (1−t)^m and continuous density on the contact set. Compactness gives pointwise upper limit bounded by the original section density, with uniform bounded support for reverse Fatou. Moving both endpoint bases toward the same interior base also moves their interpolant toward that base, so the limiting inequality follows for all positive-mass endpoints. Convexity gives a positive-volume interpolated section. A zero-mass endpoint makes the quasiconcavity lower bound zero.

overlap.comparison: Uses strict Borell–Brascamp–Lieb for the special projective pushforward of ordinary volume, with output exponent −1/(r+1). The strict-exponent mechanism overlaps, but that fact's hypotheses and conclusion do not include the critical β=1 theorem for general bounded continuous inverse-power densities, or the contact application with its closed boundary fibers.
A particular finite projective shadow has a quasiconcave density. It does not yield continuous marginalization of inverse powers or the boundary passage.

readability: The closure argument in the last paragraph is written for full tangent projection and applies verbatim to the remaining tangent coordinates after a partial projection.

summary: The bounded one-coordinate marginal is continuous and obeys the claimed exponents, including the critical case. The closed contact application extends the full marginal inequality to the relative boundary.
